hints: Factor out $9^{1/2} = 3$ to write the expression as $3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{1/2}$.
Use the binomial expansion formula $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2}u^2 + \dots$ with $n = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $u = -\dfrac{x}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Factor out $9^{1/2}$ so the binomial expression has a leading term of $1$:
$$(9 - 3x)^{1/2} = \left(9\left(1 - \dfrac{3x}{9}\right)\right)^{1/2} = 9^{1/2}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{1/2} = 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{1/2}$$

Use the binomial series expansion $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots$ with $n = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $u = -\dfrac{x}{3}$:
$$\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{1/2} = 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - 1\right)}{2}\left(-\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2 + \dots$$

Simplify each coefficient inside the bracket:
$$\text{Term 1} = 1$$
$$\text{Term 2} = -\dfrac{x}{6}$$
$$\text{Term 3} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{2}\left(\dfrac{x^2}{9}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{x^2}{9}\right) = -\dfrac{x^2}{72}$$

Multiply the series expansion through by the outer factor of $3$:
$$3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{6}x - \dfrac{1}{72}x^2 + \dots\right) = 3 - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{6}x\right) - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{72}x^2\right) = 3 - \dfrac{1}{2}x - \dfrac{1}{24}x^2$$
